surfaces.name: Fleet engine and fleet CLI (headless, same repository)

claims.answer: Terminal interface (thurbox) and CLIs (thurbox-cli, fleet) for macOS arm64, Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64; no GUI desktop app, web client or phone app; sessions are controlled by keyboard in the TUI or by fleet verbs from any shell.

desktop_os.answer: Release archives exist for aarch64-apple-darwin, Linux x64 (gnu/musl) and arm64 (musl) and x86_64 Windows (needs psmux); these are terminal programs, not a GUI desktop app; Intel macOS has no archive; minimum OS versions not stated.

mobile_apps.answer: No iOS or Android app in a bounded search.

browser.answer: No browser client; website is documentation.

cli.answer: `thurbox-cli` (doctor, update, version) and `fleet` (init, up, apply, list, get, send, watch, delete, amend, signal, result, declare, event, gateway).

editor_extensions.answer: `Ctrl+O` opens a session folder in an editor; no editor extension (v2 satellite panes are separate repos).

task_actions.answer: Create (Ctrl+N), rename, reorder, delete, search, send text, steer in the live agent pane, shell pane toggle and fleet verbs.

notifications.answer: OS notifications on attention/idle transitions with click-to-focus on Linux.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Fleets over ssh/WSL let one interface list sessions on several machines; sessions outlive the interface; no phone or web handoff.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: desktop_os, mobile_apps, browser, mobile_browser, editor_extensions, cross_device_continuity; see atomic answers.

claims.answer: Runs nine unmodified agent CLIs through Fleet harness profiles inside tmux/psmux terminals; new agents are TOML profiles; no embedded harness or model-provider layer.

harnesses.answer: Claude Code, Codex, pi, opencode, kilo, omp, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot CLI and Kimi Code; README also names "any CLI you describe yourself" via harness profiles.

model_providers.answer: Model choice is the agent CLI; `spec.model` is passed to harnesses and refused by runtimes that pass no model.

custom_adapters.answer: A harness profile is a TOML file under harnesses/ in Fleet config (command, args, resume argv, status hooks).

session_integration.answer: Launches each agent command in a tmux window (psmux on Windows) and watches status through hooks and screen rules; no API control of the model loop.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Sessions of different harnesses are listed together and each Task chooses its harness.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: model_providers; see atomic answers.

claims.answer: Agents are launched unmodified and use their own logins and API keys; thurbox has no accounts, credits or billing.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Each agent CLI uses its own login (the screenshots show Claude Code asking /login); thurbox adds nothing.

api_accounts.answer: Agent CLIs use their own API keys; `env`/EnvProvider can inject environment values.

vendor_credits.answer: No vendor credits or paid plans exist.

local_models.answer: Possible only through agent CLIs that support them (opencode, pi); thurbox adds no local-model runtime.

account_switching.answer: Per-Task `env` and TaskConfig can point an agent at different config directories or keys; no account switcher.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider terms on third-party harness use are not documented by thurbox.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: vendor_credits, local_models, account_switching, provider_restrictions; see atomic answers.
claims.unknownReason: Provider terms are external policies, not in the repository.

claims.answer: Install script, `thurbox-cli doctor`, run `thurbox`; first launch runs `fleet init`; needs tmux ≥3.2 (psmux on Windows), git and an agent CLI; remote machines via ssh or WSL Fleets; no managed cloud.

first_task_setup.answer: README First steps: doctor, thurbox, Ctrl+N picks Fleet, place, repository, agent; installer puts five programs on PATH.

no_git.answer: A directory that is no git repository gets a plain directory workspace URL instead of a worktree URL.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Worktrees are created locally from git-repository workspace URLs.

hosted_git.answer: Forge adapters (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) cover change requests; repositories can be cloned from `git+https` URLs.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: README lists tmux ≥3.2 or psmux ≥3.3.8, git and an agent CLI; `thurbox-cli doctor` checks each Fleet, runtime and agents.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Documented setup: run `fleet up` as a user service (systemd unit given) on the box and list it under [fleets.<name>] with ssh transport.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: hosted_git, managed_cloud_setup; see atomic answers.

claims.answer: Fleet CLI and a declarative resource store expose create, inspect, send, watch, result and delete operations; no network API, SDK, MCP server or webhooks into Fleet.

cli.answer: `fleet` verbs: apply, list, get, send, amend, watch --json, delete, signal, result, declare, event, runtime, gateway, doctor.

api.answer: Resources are `apiVersion: fleet/v1alpha1` files in a local store reached through the CLI; no HTTP API.

sdk.answer: No SDK; plugin programs speak a documented plugin protocol.

webhooks.answer: Gateway receives chat messages from Slack and Discord; no general webhook endpoint.

authentication.answer: Local file-store with a lease and compare-and-swap; remote Fleets reached over the user ssh/WSL login; chat tokens in operator-owned curl configs.

stability.answer: Resources are `v1alpha1`; a Fleet lacking fleet/v1alpha1 is refused; README says v3 is not yet stable.

limitations: Not fully established or not supported: api, sdk, mcp_server, webhooks, stability; see atomic answers.

evidence.title: GitHub repository metadata
evidence.finding: 120 stars, MIT, homepage thurbox.thurbeen.eu, Rust, pushed 2026-11-17.

evidence.title: Release v3.5.2 and assets
evidence.finding: Latest release v3.5.2 (2026-11-17) with archives for aarch64-apple-darwin, aarch64/x86_64 Linux (musl; gnu x64) and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc plus sha256 sums.

evidence.title: README
evidence.locator: intro; Use v2 for now; What's new in v3; Install v3; First steps
evidence.finding: Terminal workspace running Claude Code, Codex, pi, opencode, kilo, omp, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI and Kimi Code unmodified; sessions outlive the interface; Fleets over ssh/WSL; worktree per session; Lua panes; MIT; v3 not yet fully stable.

evidence.title: Where sessions run
evidence.locator: Terms; Today and planned; What thurbox does on another machine
evidence.finding: Fleets and places (local, ssh, WSL); remote Fleet session panes; diffs and git stats refuse remote sessions; VM runtime planned.

evidence.title: Orchestration
evidence.locator: Every Task is a session; Driving sessions; Read the state; Recurring work
evidence.finding: Tasks created by scripts, agents or timers appear in the list; parent label nests workers under a lead; fleet list/get/apply/send/watch/delete verbs.

evidence.title: Agents
evidence.locator: bundled harness table; How status works
evidence.finding: Nine bundled harness profiles with hooks and screen rules; status working/attention/idle/unknown; new agents are TOML harness profiles.

evidence.title: Fleet overview
evidence.finding: Declarative engine: Task, TaskConfig, EnvProvider, ChangeRequest, Conversation, Listener, Board, CronTask, plugin kinds; controllers reconcile; compare-and-swap store under a lease.

evidence.title: Task resource
evidence.finding: Task spec: harness, host, model, configRef, env, pauseAfterMs, brief, amendments, workspace URLs, dispatch, outputs, forge, subscriptions; dispatch false holds the Task.

evidence.title: Task controller
evidence.locator: Retries and recovery; After a host reboot; Signals; Harness profiles
evidence.finding: Bounded retries (3 attempts, 30 s), revive of lost sessions after reboot with the same id and worktree, idle pause/resume, proven-delivery journal, per-harness hooks.

evidence.title: CronTask resource
evidence.finding: CronTask creates a Task from a template on a cron schedule with concurrencyPolicy, startingDeadlineSeconds and historyLimit.

evidence.title: Feature decisions
evidence.locator: Scheduling work; Session Lifecycle; Update Notifications; OS Notifications; Parent Sessions
evidence.finding: Fleet schedules; version_check and auto_update feature flags on by default; OS notifications; parent label nests children.

evidence.title: Forge controller
evidence.finding: Workers declare changes with `fleet declare`; ForgeController relays checks, reviews and notes to the Task inbox and can mark a draft ready by policy.

evidence.title: ChangeRequest controller
evidence.finding: Forge adapters: GitHub via gh, GitLab via glab, Azure DevOps via az, Bitbucket Cloud via curl.

evidence.title: Gateway adapters
evidence.finding: Slack and Discord adapters (Telegram and Teams mapped on paper only) let a chat thread start and talk to a Task; Fleet holds no credentials.

evidence.title: Board resource
evidence.finding: Boards are shared event logs that Tasks can subscribe to, with retention limits.

evidence.title: Fleet configuration
evidence.locator: running fleet up; forge; gateway accounts
evidence.finding: fleet init/doctor/up; accounts keep tokens in operator-owned curl config files; Fleet never reads PATs or tokens.

evidence.title: Observability
evidence.finding: No program has its own telemetry setting; OpenTelemetry export follows standard OTEL_* variables and is off without them.

evidence.title: thurbox architecture
evidence.finding: Fleet is the engine (ADR-41); the interface reads fleet watch and draws it; Lua panes.

evidence.title: runtime-mux
evidence.finding: Runtime keeps sessions alive in tmux (psmux on Windows) and makes worktrees through workspace-git.

evidence.title: Writing a pane
evidence.finding: Panes are Lua files with a sandboxed API exposing sessions, tasks, diffs and links; F10 reloads.

evidence.title: thurbox config
evidence.finding: settings.toml [features] and [fleets.<name>] with local, ssh and WSL transports.

evidence.title: Session diff worker
evidence.finding: Per-session diff computed on a background thread via git, capped at 4 MiB and exposed to Lua plugins; there is no bundled diff pane in ui/plugins.

evidence.title: Bundled interface plugins
evidence.finding: Bundled panes: sessions, agent, confirm, rename, menu, search, new_session.

evidence.title: Install script
evidence.finding: Downloads release archives and checksums and installs thurbox, thurbox-cli, fleet, runtime-mux and workspace-git.

evidence.title: LICENSE
evidence.finding: MIT License.

evidence.title: Cargo.toml
evidence.finding: Rust workspace with fleet-* crates, runtime-mux, workspace-git, thurbox; MIT.

evidence.title: Interface demo animation
evidence.finding: First frame: Sessions list (fix-osc52-tmux, perf-session-order-cache, add-wsl-host-tests, docs-remote-hooks), Claude Code pane, Tasks list (3 open) and System CPU/MEM panel.

evidence.title: Bounded search: MCP and API servers
evidence.locator: grep mcp|model context protocol over crates/, ui/, docs/
evidence.finding: No MCP server or HTTP API is shipped; the only match is a harness MCP-reload status string.

evidence.title: Bounded search: SSO and accounts
evidence.finding: No SSO, accounts or multi-user model; matches concern forge organizations only.

evidence.title: Bounded search: cost and usage
evidence.locator: grep token usage|cost|spend|billing over crates/, docs/
evidence.finding: No per-task cost or token accounting; matches are tests and theme code.

evidence.title: Bounded search: container and sandbox isolation
evidence.finding: No container, VM or OS sandbox for agents; matches are tmux/workspace code and test sandboxes; VM runtime is planned only.

evidence.title: Bounded search: web and mobile clients
evidence.locator: grep web ui|browser client|http server|ios|android over crates/, website/
evidence.finding: No web client or phone app; the interface is a terminal UI (website is documentation).
